newsitem.title: USA: Guyana president in stable condition in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Guyana president in stable condition in U.S..

text.p: Guyana's President Cheddi Jagan is in stable condition after U.S. doctors cleared a blocked artery, hospital and embassy officials said on Tuesday.

A spokesman for Walter Reed Army Medical Centre near Washington said Jagan was in stable condition and under observation. An embassy spokeswoman said "the next 72 hours are critical" and that Jagan's family was optimistic.

Doctors performed a procedure called angioplasty where a surgical balloon is inserted into an artery and then inflated to clear any blockage. Jagan, 78, was taken by U.S. military plane to Washington on Saturday for medical tests after being taken to a hospital suffering from heart problems.

Jagan led his People's Progressive Party (PPP) to victory at the polls in October 1992 -- Guyana's first democratic elections for 28 years. He was premier of British Guiana from 1961 to 1964 before Guyana gained independence in 1966.
